source_title: Why Gap Inc pulled the plug on Old Navy's spin off
publisher_issuer: Fortune; corroborated by Fast Company and Gap Inc. SEC filings (CIK 0000039911)
company_context: Gap Inc. is a large U.S. apparel retailer with the Old Navy, Gap, Banana Republic, and Athleta brands. In February 2019 it announced a plan to split into two public companies, spinning off Old Navy (its strongest brand) from the rest. By early 2020, weakening performance led the board to abandon the split, leaving a mixed, multi-year restructuring outcome.
macro_context: Mall-traffic decline, fast-fashion and e-commerce disruption, and weakening specialty-apparel performance; activist and strategic pressure to unlock value via separation.
evidence_summary: Old Navy generated about $8 billion of Gap Inc.'s revenue in 2018 versus ~$9 billion for the rest of the portfolio, and the Gap brand had shrunk from ~$7.2 billion (2004) to ~$5.16 billion (2018). Gap announced the Old Navy spin-off in February 2019, but in the three quarters that followed Old Navy itself posted comparable-sales declines of roughly 1% to 5%. On January 16-17, 2020 the board cancelled the separation, citing the cost and complexity of splitting plus softer business performance, a reversal of the announced strategy that left the company intact but in continued multi-brand restructuring.
owner_decision_context: Gap Inc.'s board first decided to separate Old Navy to unlock value, then reversed course when Old Navy's performance softened and the structural cost of separation outweighed the benefit.
action_taken: Announced (Feb 2019) then cancelled (Jan 2020) the Old Navy spin-off, reversing a major strategic-separation decision and retaining the multi-brand structure while continuing restructuring.
outcome_evidence: The cancellation statement cited 'the cost and complexity of splitting into two companies, combined with softer business performance'; Old Navy comparable sales fell ~1-5% post-announcement and the Gap brand continued its long decline, producing a mixed, partial-recovery trajectory rather than a clean turnaround.
source_limitations: WebFetch unavailable (403 pattern); figures confirmed across Fortune, Fast Company, Business of Fashion, and Gap Inc. SEC 8-K filings (CIK 0000039911) via WebSearch snippets. Brand-level revenue figures are reported approximations from named journalism citing company results.
directly_stated: Old Navy had ~$8 billion revenue in 2018; rest of Gap portfolio ~$9 billion
Gap brand sales fell from ~$7.2 billion (2004) to ~$5.16 billion (2018)
Old Navy posted comparable-sales declines of ~1-5% after the announcement
Board cited cost/complexity of separation plus softer performance
inferred: The reversed separation indicates a strategic miscalculation followed by partial correction (mixed outcome)
Underlying demand softness, not just structure, drove the abandonment
why_useful_for_opsiq: Outcome-5 mixed/partial case: a major strategic-separation decision announced then reversed, with continued restructuring. Tests whether the engine handles ambiguous multi-year outcomes and recognizes a reversed strategic action without forcing a clean failure/turnaround label.
